chapter.name: Oceans and Continents
chapter.blurb: About three-fourths of Earth's surface is water, mostly in five interconnected oceans (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic); the rest is land, organised into continents, counted anywhere from four to seven depending on convention (seven is standard). Oceans drive climate and disasters (monsoons, cyclones, tsunamis), support islands like Greenland and India's own island groups, and sustain life globally through oxygen production, though they face pollution and overfishing threats.

scope_in.item: About three-fourths of Earth's surface is water (mostly oceans), a little over one-fourth is land; a large body of land is a landmass, a large continuous expanse of land is a continent; the Northern Hemisphere has more land than the Southern Hemisphere

The five oceans -- Pacific (largest), Atlantic, Indian, Southern/Antarctic, Arctic (smallest) -- are interconnected, with boundaries between them being human conventions; the Indian Ocean is bordered by Asia (north), Africa (west), Australia (east); it includes the Arabian Sea (west of India) and Bay of Bengal (east of India)

Oceans bring monsoon rains but also cause cyclones (violent storms) and tsunamis (huge waves from undersea earthquakes/volcanic eruptions); the 26 December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (from an Indonesian earthquake) killed over two lakh people across 14 countries, severely affecting Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; early warning systems (Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System) and India's National Disaster Management Authority help manage such disasters

Continents can be counted as four, five, six or seven depending on how adjoining landmasses (North/South America; Europe/Asia as 'Eurasia'; Africa/Eurasia) are grouped; seven is the most widely used count (Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, South America); the five Olympic rings represent the five inhabited continents (Africa, America, Asia, Australia, Europe)

An island is a smaller landmass surrounded by water (continents are too large to be called islands); Greenland is the world's largest island, about the size of India's 10 largest states combined; India has over 1,300 islands, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Bay of Bengal) and Lakshadweep Islands (Arabian Sea); the Indian Antarctica Programme (since 1981) and its first base Dakshin Gangotri (1983) support scientific research on climate/environment in Antarctica's harsh climate

Oceans sustain life: their flora produces over half the world's oxygen ('the planet's lungs'); oceans enable rain/water cycle, migration, trade, military campaigns, fishing, and have shaped coastal cultures/legends; World Oceans Day is 8 June; oceans face threats from plastic pollution (millions of tonnes yearly) and overfishing

concepts.name: Oceans and continents: proportions and hemispheric distribution
concepts.description: Water covers about three-fourths of Earth's surface (mostly oceans), land a little over one-fourth, unevenly split between the hemispheres.
concepts.idea: About three-fourths of the Earth's surface is covered by water (mostly oceans) and a little over one-fourth is land, unevenly distributed between hemispheres.
concepts.rule: A large body of land is a landmass, a large continuous expanse of land is a continent; the Northern Hemisphere has more land than the Southern Hemisphere.
concepts.example: Seen from space, the Earth looks mostly blue because of its oceans, earning it the nickname the blue planet.

questions.q: Explain why the term 'landmass' is a more general term than 'continent,' based on how the chapter uses these words.

s: States the claim is not well supported

concepts.name: The five oceans: names, sizes and boundaries
concepts.description: Five interconnected oceans (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic) with conventional boundaries; the Indian Ocean borders India via the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.
concepts.idea: There are five oceans -- Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic -- not truly separate, since seawater flows between them.
concepts.rule: In decreasing size: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic; the Indian Ocean is bordered by Asia, Africa and Australia, including the Arabian Sea (west of India) and Bay of Bengal (east of India).
concepts.example: A drop of water from the Pacific can eventually mix into the Atlantic, since the oceans are interconnected, not divided by fixed walls.

concepts.name: Oceans and life: oxygen, human uses, and pollution
